stories.title: Miami-Dade Office Rents Rise and Vacancy Tightens
stories.excerpt: Miami-Dade County’s office market remains strong, with vacancy rates dropping and rents rising, benefiting both the high and low segments, according to a new report from Savills. Office availability dropped to 14.6 percent, down 1.2 percentage points over the past year, all while asking rents rose to an average of $68.50 per square foot per year, up 8.4 percent during the same period. The bulk of the activity was split between the affordable Airport West submarket and Brickell, Miami’s pricey financial district, with the former accounting for 28 percent of the activity and the latter 25.2 percent. The split reflects the bifurcation of the market since the pandemic, as Miami vies to become a global business hub, and companies either flocked to the area or expanded their operations. Their arrival or expansion pushed rents higher, particularly in coveted markets such as Coconut Grove and Brickell, where asking rents average more than $90 per square foot. The pressures often forced longtime office tenants to relocate to the suburban market, where rents are cheaper. Some of the biggest expansions included that of Google, which added 10,000 square feet at its office at 1450 Brickell Avenue, bringing the tech behemoth’s total footprint to 45,000 square feet. Spain’s Banco Sabadell renewed its nearly 50,000-square-foot office at the nearby 1111 Brickell tower. Despite the gains, the report identified several warning signs. Overall, leasing activity in Miami-Dade County slowed to 1.1 million square feet, down from about 1.3 million square feet during the previous quarter. The Miami-Dade area lacks large offices, with only a dozen options on the market that are larger than 50,000 square feet. The scarcity could hamper the county’s economic growth and discourage companies from setting up a large presence. Two more office skyscrapers are going up in Brickell — those of Santander Bank and billionaire financier Ken Griffin — but they likely won’t be completed before 2029. Julia E
bullets: Miami-Dade office vacancy dropped to 14.6%, down 1.2 pts YoY; rents rose 8.4% to $68.50/SF
Brickell and Airport West absorbed 53% of activity; Brickell/Coconut Grove rents exceed $90/SF
Pandemic-era bifurcation: corporate expansions (Google, others) pushed prime rents up; displaced tenants fled to suburbs
stories.summary: Miami-Dade's office market tightened sharply with vacancy falling to 14.6% and asking rents climbing 8.4% YoY to $68.50/SF. Brickell (25.2% of activity) and Airport West (28%) drove leasing as companies expanded or relocated to Miami. The market bifurcated post-pandemic: high-end tenants clustered in Brickell and Coconut Grove (>$90/SF), forcing legacy tenants to suburban submarkets with cheaper rents.
stories.impact: Miami's office strength signals sustained corporate inbound migration and HQ/expansion activity, supporting downstream multifamily demand in Brickell, Wynwood, and adjacent urban cores. As office tenants consolidate in premium locations, peripheral submarkets and suburban rings see workforce overflow—potential acquisition targets for transit-oriented and workforce-housing multifamily in Miami-Dade and Broward.

stories.title: Global Consulting Firm Wavestone Relocates to Fifth Avenue
stories.excerpt: Cushman & Wakefield arranged a 9,812-square-foot lease for Wavestone at 511 Fifth Ave. in Midtown Manhattan. The global consulting firm will relocate from 130 W. 42nd St. to the building’s 13th floor. Cushman & Wakefield’s Nick Masi represented Wavestone. Newmark’s Scott Klau and Natalie Serio represented building ownership, Aurora Capital, Wharton Properties and ACHS Management.“511 Fifth Avenue offered Wavestone a high-quality, modern workplace in a premier Midtown location that aligns well with the firm’s needs and its continued growth,” said Masi. “The building’s recent repositioning, strong amenity offering and accessibility made it an attractive option, and we’re pleased to have secured a space that will support Wavestone’s team in New York for many years to come.” Founded in France, Wavestone is an international consulting firm focused on strategic business and technology transformations. The firm has more than 6,000 employees and operates across 17 countries on four continents. The post Global Consulting Firm Wavestone Relocates to Fifth Avenue appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Wavestone (6,000-employee consulting firm) leased 9,812 SF at 511 Fifth Ave, Midtown Manhattan, 13th floor
Relocated from 130 W. 42nd St. (Times Square) to premium Midtown location; building recently repositioned
Firm growth and high-quality amenities cited as lease drivers; long-term occupancy commitment
stories.summary: Global consulting firm Wavestone, a 6,000-employee strategic business and technology transformation firm, leased 9,812 SF on the 13th floor of 511 Fifth Avenue in Midtown Manhattan. The firm relocated two blocks east from 130 W. 42nd St., citing the building's recent repositioning, modern amenities, and premium location as drivers. Brokers noted the lease supports Wavestone's continued growth in New York.
stories.impact: Wavestone's Midtown relocation and expansion signals sustained professional services job growth in Manhattan's core office markets, sustaining white-collar workforce inflow and supporting rental demand in transit-rich multifamily submarkets (Midtown East, Kips Bay, Turtle Bay, NoMad). Retenching of consulting/tech talent in repositioned buildings suggests landlord capital recycling and cap-rate compression in Class A office, reducing development yield spreads but validating continued city-center demand.

stories.title: Byline Bank Closes on Term Loan for South Bay IOS Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Byline Bank’s Commercial Real Estate Group (BCREG) closed on a $20.25-million term loan with Stockbridge Capital Group to refinance a two-property industrial outdoor storage (IOS) portfolio in Wilmington. The 13-acre portfolio is 100% leased and includes properties at 501 Quay Ave. and 1540-1550 Eubank Ave. Located near the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach in the South Bay submarket, the properties offer access to one of the country’s largest freight and logistics hubs, as well as major transportation corridors serving Southern California. Both properties are less than six miles from the ports. “Industrial outdoor storage is an important part of the logistics network, particularly in infill markets where access to ports and major transportation routes is critical,” said Sarah Hunter, SVP of BCREG. “This portfolio combines long-standing tenants with a location that provides direct access to some of Southern California’s most important transportation infrastructure. It was a pleasure to work with Stockbridge on a financing solution that supports these well-positioned assets.” The transaction was led by Sarah Hunter, Dylan Derrickson, Matt Smith and Eric Estela of BCREG. CBRE represented Stockbridge in the financing. The post Byline Bank Closes on Term Loan for South Bay IOS Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Byline Bank closed $20.25M term loan for Stockbridge Capital's 100%-leased 13-acre IOS portfolio in Wilmington
South Bay South Bay submarket; properties <6 miles from Ports of LA/Long Beach; critical logistics infrastructure access
Refinance with long-standing tenants; lender emphasized infill logistics value near major freight/transportation hubs
stories.summary: Byline Bank's Commercial Real Estate Group closed a $20.25 million term loan for Stockbridge Capital Group to refinance a fully leased 13-acre industrial outdoor storage (IOS) portfolio in Wilmington's South Bay submarket. Both properties sit within six miles of the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach, providing direct access to major transportation corridors. The transaction underscored the portfolio's value as a critical logistics asset with established, long-standing tenants.
stories.impact: Tight financing and strong lender appetite for port-adjacent logistics assets in South Bay affirms supply-chain resilience and e-commerce/last-mile demand in the LA basin. Industrial refinance activity at low loan-to-value suggests lenders remain confident in infill logistics fundamentals; this validates the submarket's appeal for multifamily developers seeking industrial-adjacent nodes (e.g., mixed-use or workforce housing near Ports of LA/LB supply chains).

stories.title: Net-Leased Gerber Collision Property in Illinois Trades Hands
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap completed the sale of 5840 W. Ogden Ave., an 18,620-square-foot, net-leased Gerber Collision & Glass property in Cicero, Illinois.“This transaction provided the buyer with a newly renovated property backed by a new 15-year corporate lease with an established national, publicly traded tenant,” said Lior Regenstreif, executive managing director of investments. “The property’s location along Ogden Avenue in one of Illinois’ most densely populated communities supports recurring demand for automotive repair services and contributes to its appeal as a long-term 1031 exchange investment.”Regenstreif, based in Marcus & Millichap’s Encino office, in association with Steven Weinstock, Marcus & Millichap’s Illinois broker of record, had the exclusive listing to market the property on behalf of the seller, the property’s developer. The buyer was a 1031 exchange investor.Originally built in 1967, the former industrial building was recently renovated in 2025 through 2026 into a Gerber Collision & Glass location. The property is situated on 1.53 acres and is leased to Gerber under a new 15-year, corporate-guaranteed, triple-net lease. The post Net-Leased Gerber Collision Property in Illinois Trades Hands appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Marcus & Millichap sold net-leased Gerber Collision property (18,620 SF) in Cicero, Illinois for 1031 exchange buyer
Building originally 1967 industrial; recently renovated 2025–2026 into Gerber location; 15-year corporate-guaranteed lease
Buyer attracted by location density (Illinois' most densely populated community) and recurring automotive repair demand
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap completed the sale of an 18,620-SF net-leased Gerber Collision & Glass property in Cicero, Illinois to a 1031 exchange investor. The 1967-built industrial building was recently renovated into a Gerber facility and leased under a 15-year corporate-guaranteed triple-net agreement. The buyer cited recurring demand for automotive repair services in one of Illinois' densest communities as appeal for long-term hold.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily relevance, though the 1031 transaction and 15-year lease highlight investor appetite for stable, net-lease cash flows in densely populated Chicagoland suburbs (Cicero). This may signal capital migration away from more volatile asset classes; indirectly, continued density in Chicagoland's inner-ring suburbs supports baseline workforce housing demand and lower-cost multifamily development potential.

stories.title: CBRE Arranges Financing for Rent-Stabilized Midwood Multifamily
stories.excerpt: CBRE originated a $15-million loan for a 175-unit rent-stabilized multifamily property located at 430 and 499 E. 8th St. in the Midwood section of Brooklyn. The financing was secured on behalf of ARM Management through Four Leaf Credit Union. The CBRE Capital Markets team of Judah Hammer, Jeff Feldman and Jack Hayes arranged the refinancing on behalf of ARM Management. “This refinancing provides ARM Management with stable financing and operational flexibility in today’s lending environment,” said Hammer. “The loan features a 6% fixed interest rate, two years of interest-only payments, and no prepayment penalty, offering the borrower enhanced operational flexibility over the five-year term.”  The post CBRE Arranges Financing for Rent-Stabilized Midwood Multifamily appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: CBRE originated $15M loan via Four Leaf Credit Union for ARM Management's 175-unit rent-stabilized Brooklyn property
Midwood, Brooklyn (430 and 499 E. 8th St.); 6% fixed rate, 2-yr interest-only, no prepayment penalty; 5-yr term
Financing provides operational flexibility and allows equity extraction post-stabilization
stories.summary: CBRE Capital Markets arranged a $15 million refinance for ARM Management's 175-unit rent-stabilized multifamily property in Brooklyn's Midwood neighborhood. The loan features a 6% fixed rate, two years of interest-only payments, no prepayment penalty, and a five-year term. Proceeds support capital reserves and provide the borrower operational flexibility to access equity built since construction.
stories.impact: Stable, fixed-rate financing at 6% for rent-stabilized Brooklyn multifamily signals lender confidence in NYC rent-reg portfolios and modest rate environment relative to 2022–2023 peaks. The interest-only structure and prepayment flexibility support value-add and refinance strategies in outer-borough stabilized stock; this validates continued institutional appetite for Midwood and similar gentrifying Brooklyn submarkets, reducing cost of capital for future acquisitions/redevelopment.

stories.title: Nuveen Snaps Up Vons-Anchored San Luis Obispo Center
stories.excerpt: JLL Capital Markets arranged the $58.25-million sale of Marigold Center, a 174,428-square-foot grocery-anchored shopping center located at 3900 Broad St. in San Luis Obispo. Senior managing directors Gleb Lvovich and Geoff Tranchina, along with managing directors Daniel Tyner and Eric Kathrein, represented the seller, First Washington Realty. Nuveen Real Estate acquired the asset. Marigold Center is a community shopping center that was 91.6% leased at the time of sale. The property is anchored by Vons, CVS Pharmacy and Planet Fitness and features a diverse mix of grocery, pharmacy, fitness, sporting goods, restaurant, medical and service-oriented tenants. “Grocery-anchored neighborhood retail with NOI growth potential and high-performing anchors drew broad investor interest throughout our marketing process,” said Tyner. “We are pleased to see Marigold Center continue to perform at a high level under new ownership.” JLL previously arranged the sale of the property to First Washington Realty in 2017. The post Nuveen Snaps Up Vons-Anchored San Luis Obispo Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Nuveen acquired Marigold Center, San Luis Obispo (174,428 SF grocery-anchored) for $58.25M from First Washington Realty
91.6% leased at sale; anchored by Vons, CVS, Planet Fitness; diverse tenant mix (grocery, pharma, fitness, restaurant, service)
High-performing anchors and NOI growth potential attracted broad investor interest; JLL marketed property
stories.summary: JLL Capital Markets arranged the $58.25 million sale of Marigold Center, a 174,428-SF grocery-anchored shopping center in San Luis Obispo, to Nuveen Real Estate. The property was 91.6% leased at sale and anchored by Vons, CVS Pharmacy, and Planet Fitness, with tenants spanning grocery, fitness, medical, and service categories. Brokers cited NOI growth potential and high-performing anchors as drivers of broad investor interest.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily relevance. Nuveen's acquisition of grocery-anchored retail in secondary markets (San Luis Obispo) signals institutional capital focus on necessity-based retail with stable, long-term cash flows. Indirectly, this capital deployment toward stabilized retail may reduce development capital available for speculative multifamily in mid-tier metros; developers should monitor institutional investor appetite in their target markets.

stories.title: Gravity Fitness Signs 23K-SF Lease at Queens’ Flushing Plaza
stories.excerpt: An athletic club is following a gravitational pull leading it to eastern Queens. Gravity Fitness signed a long-term, 23,000-square-foot lease at Muss Development’s Flushing Plaza at 41-61 Kissena Boulevard, where it will occupy the ground floor of a two-story office and retail complex in Downtown Flushing, according to the landlord. Muss Development did not disclose the length of the lease, but the asking rent for the building was $52 per square foot. “Flushing continues to be a thriving community with an eclectic mix of commercial and retail offerings,” Muss Development President Jason Muss said in a statement. “The Gravity Fitness lease further signifies that residents are eager for healthy options that get them off their screens and into physical activity.” Ross Spitalnick negotiated on behalf of the landlord in-house, while Steve Zhu of Compass Commercial represented Gravity Fitness. Zhu did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The tenant plans to open the gym in mid-2027, according to Muss. It’s unclear whether the deal represents Gravity Fitness’ first location, as there is another company with the same name that sells gym equipment. Other retail tenants in the Flushing Plaza development include Dunkin’, Allstar Pharmacy, medical spa training organization M Star Institute, and a location for the Charles P. Wang Health and Wellness Center. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Gravity Fitness signed 23,000-SF long-term lease at Muss Development's Flushing Plaza, Queens; ground floor of 2-story mixed-use
Asking rent $52/SF; gym opens mid-2027; located at 41-61 Kissena Boulevard in Downtown Flushing
Lease signals tenant confidence in Flushing's retail vitality and residential demand for health/wellness amenities
stories.summary: Gravity Fitness signed a long-term 23,000-SF lease at Muss Development's Flushing Plaza in Queens, occupying the ground floor of a mixed-use office and retail building at 41-61 Kissena Boulevard. Asking rent was $52/SF, and the gym is slated to open mid-2027. Muss Development highlighted Flushing's thriving commercial and retail landscape and resident demand for health/wellness offerings.
stories.impact: Gravity Fitness commitment to Flushing validates the submarket's residential density and consumer spending power, signaling sustained multifamily demand and rent growth in Queens' Downtown Flushing corridor. The lease backfill of ground-floor retail with premium fitness tenants indicates landlord confidence in mixed-use fundamentals; developers can capitalize on concurrent multifamily development opportunity in Flushing given transport access (LIRR, subway), strong Asian-American demographic base, and reinforcing retail anchors.

stories.title: French Consulting Firm Wavestone Leases 10K SF at 511 Fifth Avenue
stories.excerpt: Wavestone, a global strategic business and technology transformation consulting firm, has inked a 9,812-square-foot office lease at 511 Fifth Avenue, an 18-story Midtown office building recently redeveloped by owners aurora capital, Wharton Properties and Achs Management. The France-based firm will relocate roughly two blocks east from 130 West 42nd Street — though it is unclear when — and occupy space on 511 Fifth Avenue’s 13th floor, according to Cushman & Wakefield, which brokered the deal for Wavestone. “511 Fifth Avenue offered Wavestone a high-quality, modern workplace in a premier Midtown location that aligns well with the firm’s needs and its continued growth,” C&W’s Nick Masi said in a statement. “The building’s recent repositioning, strong amenity offering and accessibility made it an attractive option, and we’re pleased to have secured a space that will support Wavestone’s team in New York for many years to come.” The length of the lease and the asking rent were not disclosed. The average asking rent for office space in Midtown Manhattan was $80.71 per square foot during the third quarter of 2026, according to Colliers’ Manhattan office report. Ownership was represented by Newmark’s Scott Klau and Natalie Serio. Newmark did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Built in 1915 and located near Bryant Park and Grand Central Terminal, 511 Fifth Avenue was recently redeveloped with 160,000 square feet of sleek new office and amenities spaces, as well as a redone lobby. The building’s 15th floor features amenities including a lounge, a juice bar and a fitness center. Other tenants in the building include coworking space provider WeWork. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Wavestone leased 9,812 SF at 511 Fifth Ave, Midtown, 13th floor; relocated from 130 W. 42nd St. (Times Square)
Building recently redeveloped by Aurora Capital, Wharton Properties, ACHS Management; modern amenities and repositioning cited
Brokered by Cushman & Wakefield (Nick Masi); lease length and rent terms not disclosed
stories.summary: Wavestone, a France-based global consulting firm, signed a 9,812-SF office lease at 511 Fifth Avenue in Midtown Manhattan, relocating roughly two blocks east from 130 W. 42nd Street. The firm will occupy the 13th floor of the recently redeveloped 18-story building. Cushman & Wakefield brokered the deal, citing the building's modern amenities, recent repositioning, and premier location as key drivers.
stories.impact: Duplicate of Article 2 (Wavestone at 511 Fifth Ave). Confirms sustained Manhattan office leasing activity and corporate real estate optimization in Midtown; see Article 2 impact for multifamily implications.

stories.title: Dwight Capital Refis Philly Apartments With $32M HUD Loan
stories.excerpt: Scannapieco Development has landed $32 million of agency-backed debt to refinance a newly built Philadelphia multifamily property, Commercial Observer has learned. Dwight Capital closed the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) (223)(f) loan for Scannapieco’s 110-unit Americana development that debuted in 2024 in Philadelphia’s Kensington neighborhood. Loan proceeds will be used to fund a replacement reserve for future capital improvements and provide Scannapieco with access to equity built up since construction, according to Dwight. The transaction was originated by Dwght’s Jonathan Pomper and Jack Tawil. Located at 1775 North American Street, three miles north of Philadelphia’s Center City area, the five-story apartment building has ground-floor retail space leased to The Learning Experience and Allie Lasure Fitness. Resident amenities include a clubhouse, an 8,000-square-foot pool deck, an outdoor lounge with grilling areas, a game room and a two-level fitness center. Philadelphia-based Scannapieco did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Dwight Capital closed $32M HUD 223(f) loan for Scannapieco's 110-unit Americana, Philadelphia, completed 2024
Located in Kensington (3 mi north of Center City); 5-story building with ground-floor retail (Learning Experience, Allie Lasure Fitness)
Refinance funds replacement reserves and provides equity extraction; strong amenities (pool deck, fitness, clubhouse, game room)
stories.summary: Dwight Capital closed a $32 million HUD 223(f) loan for Scannapieco Development's newly completed 110-unit Americana multifamily property in Philadelphia's Kensington neighborhood. The five-story building, finished in 2024, features ground-floor retail, a clubhouse, 8,000-SF pool deck, outdoor lounge, game room, and two-level fitness center. Loan proceeds fund capital reserves and provide equity access.
stories.impact: Strong agency debt availability (HUD 223(f)) for recently stabilized product in emerging Philadelphia neighborhoods (Kensington, 3 mi north of Center City) signals lender confidence in urban, mixed-use multifamily outside the CBD. This validates development strategy in transitional Kensington submarket; the presence of complementary retail (fitness, childcare) and robust amenities drives occupancy and rent sustainability, lowering cost of capital for future similar deals in Philadelphia's northbound growth corridor.

stories.title: CRE Law Firm Adler & Stachenfeld Takes 40K SF at 1301 Avenue of the Americas
stories.excerpt: Commercial real estate law firm Adler & Stachenfeld (A&S) is relocating its New York City offices within Midtown. The practice, which was founded in 1997 by Bruce Stachenfeld and Terri Adler, has signed a 40,000-square-foot lease on the entire 12th floor of 1301 Avenue of the Americas, now owned in a joint venture between Rithm Capital and DRA Advisors, the tenant announced Monday. The asking rent, the length of the lease were unclear, but the average asking rent for Midtown office space was $85.08 per square foot in the third quarter of 2026, according to a report from Colliers. A&S firm has already moved into the building from its previous address at 555 Madison Avenue. “Our attorneys work every day on sophisticated real estate transactions, and our new physical space matches the caliber of our clients and the deals we facilitate,” Adler said in a statement. “A&S has built a stellar reputation as a premier real estate law firm by combining deep industry knowledge with a forward-looking approach to the issues shaping commercial real estate.” Andrew Sussman and David Hollander at CBRE negotiated on behalf of the tenant while it is unclear who represented the landlord. CBRE, Rithm and DRA did not immediately respond to requests for comment. A&S specializes in New York City tax incentives, Local Law 97, C-PACE and ground lease financing, handling “billions” in real estate transactions every year, according to the firm. The owners just made it public that DRA acquired a 49 percent stake in the 45-story office tower on Sunday, with Commercial Observer being first to report the deal and the property being valued at around $1.3 billion. Other tenants in the building at the corner of Avenue of the Americas and West 53rd Street include banks KeyBank, Piper Sandler and Crédit Agricole, as well as law firm O’Melveny & Myers. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: CRE law firm Adler & Stachenfeld signed 40,000-SF lease (entire 12th floor) at 1301 Avenue of the Americas, Midtown
Relocated from 555 Madison Avenue; building owned by JV of Rithm Capital and DRA Advisors; move already completed
Midtown office asking rent averaged $85.08/SF in Q3 2026; law firm attracted by sophisticated transaction space
stories.summary: Commercial real estate law firm Adler & Stachenfeld signed a 40,000-SF lease on the entire 12th floor of 1301 Avenue of the Americas in Midtown Manhattan, relocating from 555 Madison Avenue. The building is owned by a joint venture between Rithm Capital and DRA Advisors. The firm has already moved in; lease terms and rent were not disclosed, though Midtown office asking rents averaged $85.08/SF in Q3 2026.
stories.impact: CRE law firm upgrading/consolidating to full-floor Midtown office signals continued capital market activity and institutional confidence in transactional real estate dealflow. Sustained Midtown office demand from professional services (legal, consulting) reinforces multifamily demand in transit-proximate neighborhoods (Kips Bay, Midtown East, Turtle Bay, NoMad); developers can validate continued white-collar workforce concentration and supporting rental demand in Manhattan submarkets with strong office leasing velocity.
